title: Do THIS First in RuneScape Dragonwilds
author: Spopes
chapters: Part 2: Getting in the Game (Trading & Account)
description:
RuneScape: Dragonwilds 1.0 is finally here! This guide breaks down everything you need to do first when loading into the full release on PC and console.

Dragonwilds is RuneScape like you’ve never experienced it before. Jagex has taken the iconic world and skills of Gielinor and evolved them into a brand-new sandbox survival crafting RPG. After a highly successful year in early access, the official 1.0 version is launching on September 15th for $29.99 with full crossplay support.

Whether you are an Old School RuneScape (OSRS) veteran or a survival game fan, this guide covers the essential day one roadmap. Learn which skills to level up fast (like Agility and Woodcutting), how to unlock melee weapon special actions at level 8 Attack, how magic and ranged combat work without a Grand Exchange, and the best practices for building your starter base to survive monster raids. Master your progression early so your squad can gear up in Rune armor and prepare for the 4-player endgame raid!

transcript.text: Dragon Wilds is Runescape like you've never experienced it before. Taking the premise and world of one of the most
enduringly popular MMOs and evolving them into a brand new survival crafting RPG, this latest project from Jagex was
only in early access for a year before launching its full 1.0 version on September 15th. Now available on console
and PC. Learn everything you need to know about Runescape Dragon Wilds 1.0 know before you jump into the full
release of this ambitious but familiar take on the increasingly popular survival RPG genre. Hey everyone, it's
Spokes. Before we get into this comprehensive yet succinct Dragons 1.0 starter guide, please like and hype the
video and subscribe if you haven't. First of all, let's briefly cover what Dragon Wilds is. I do have a more
comprehensive video on this subject that's linked above and the description. And also keep in mind I've put in time
stamps so you can skip ahead to the sections that are most important to you. But yes, Dragon Wilds is a Runescape
game, but only sort of. It's set in Gilanor, which is the same world where OSRS and Runescape 3 take place, but it
is not an MMO. Instead, it is a survival crafting game. And out of all the survival sandbox games that are out
there, it is one of the closest being an actual RPG. There are quests, the world is not procedurally generated. It has a
strong narrative to it. And both the gameplay and combat are what you're used to from an RPG. There's also a lot of
what you're used to from Runescape. A very similar skill leveling system, similar aesthetics and character models,
but the whole thing has been upgraded to Unreal Engine 5. It is the most modern and graphically polished installment in
the Runescape franchise so far. Morearm MMO like features are apparently coming with next year's update, but for now,
this is definitely a co-op RPG and nonarmmo. You can have four people at a time on your server. There is no grand
exchange. There basically is no trading at all. Put as simply as possible. Dragon Wilds is a survival crafting take
on Runescape. That should be a hit for fans of both Runescape and Survival Games. With the 1.0 version of Dragon
Wilds, there have been a lot of changes and improvements. While it's arguably the case that maybe the game should have
stayed in early access a bit longer, this is definitely a polished 1.0 product that Jagex is going to continue
evolving on as the years go by. So, now that you know what Dragon Wilds is, you need to know how to buy it. With
the 1.0 release, Dragon Wilds is now available on PC, PS5, Xbox, and Nintendo Switch 2. Previously, the game was not
available on console whatsoever, but now you can pick it up whichever console you play on, and the game does cost $29.99
on all platforms. That is rapidly becoming the standard survival RPG price tag, and the game offers quite a bit of
content for such a comparatively low price. So once you've bought and downloaded Dragon Wilds, it's time to
talk about how to actually get in the game. When you're creating a world in Dragon Wilds, you have the option making
it either private or public. With public servers, you can join other people's games, even if you're not friends with
them. Private servers are invitation only, and the maximum number of players on each server is four. You can also
choose whether to toggle crossplay on or off when you're creating a world. The game does have full crossplay as an
option, however, meaning you can play with friends whichever platform they're on. There is now also a creative version
of Dragon Wilds that is similar to creative modes in Minecraft or other games. And you have a lot more options
when you're creating a world than you used to during early access. To log in and play the game, you do
integrate your existing Jagex account. However, no items or stats or cosmetics carry over from OSRS or Runescape 3. And
something else that does not carry over is the MMO style trading system that exists in both those other games. Dragon
Wilds does not have a grand exchange or direct player-to-player trading. If you want to trade something to somebody
else, you simply drop it on the ground. Now, this will apparently be changing with the 2027 expansion. We don't have
made details yet, but this does follow the general theme of Jagex making Dragon Wilds more like an MMO as time goes by.
But yes, right now there is no traditional trading, though there is crossplay and a whole plethora of other
world creation options. So, you've gotten the game and created a world. Now, what do you do first? You're
definitely going to want to start by leveling a few core skills. You're also going to want to build your first base
and equip it with some critical stations you'll use for crafting. When it comes to which skills you should
focus on first, agility is the undisputed top priority. Leveling your agility skill increases your stamina
recovery rate, and it also allows you to move across the map in more efficient ways. So definitely take any chance you
have to level your agility. And from there, wood cutting, mining, and cooking are also essential. Obviously, combat as
well, but we'll get to that in the next section. Wood cutting and mining are how you're going to get most of the
materials you need for crafting. And then cooking is essential for managing your health and combat viability. When
it comes to wood cutting, at level 11, you unlock astral projection. There's that traditional Jagex sense of humor
front and center. So yes, not astral projection, but astral projection. And then at level 20, you unlock the ability
to clear thorny vines, which opens up hidden pathways. Leveling up mining not only allows you to get better ore, but
it also unlocks passives that help with inventory management. The higher you go up in the mining skill, the less of the
items that you mine weigh in your inventory, allowing you to carry more at a time. And then, yes, like basically
all survival RPGs, cooking is an essential part of Dragon Wilds. The more you level up that skill, the better your
recipes will get and the better the buffs that you'll unlock in your character. The good thing is that
basically all your skills just level up passively as you do things in the world.
But definitely do focus on agility, wood cutting, mining, and cooking as your top priorities.
Next, we're going to talk about building your first base. There are some simple rules for this, and keep in mind, you're
not going to stick with your first base forever. But for your very first base, which you'll need for resting and
crafting, you're going to want to build it close to a resource dense area. So anywhere there are lots of tree and ore
nodes. Like most survival games, there's gonna be a lot of foot travel, at least in the beginning. Eventually, you will
unlock mounts, but you don't have to go far when you're getting materials for upgrading your gear and crafting
stations. So, make sure that you choose a location that is next to plentiful supplies of wood and ore. Also, it's
generally best to build on high ground. As is the case in almost any situation, having the high ground will give you a
combat advantage. And then, speaking of combat advantage, you're going to want to put up defenses around your base as
quickly as possible. Monster raids are a big part of Dragon Wilds, so having a wall at least is going to keep your base
from getting vandalized or destroyed. Once you have a basic base, there are a few crafting stations you're going to
want to get as soon as you can. First and foremost is a crafting table. This is going to be the foundation of
creating your early starter tools and structures. Build a crafting table first thing once you have a usable base.
You're also going to want to have a spinning wheel and a tannery to create thread and leather armor and an armor
bench to make even better defensive sets. From there, also make a blacksmith bench to make your first metal weapons
and harvesting tools and potentially a fletching bench if you want to focus on archery. That's all stuff that goes
inside your house. But a couple stations you want to put outside but still within
your defensive perimeter are a kil and a furnace. These are going to be essential
for creating the metal bars you're going to need at your blacksmith bench. Once you've got a basic base up and
running, it's time to focus on combat. The way the game works, you can be doing melee combat at the very beginning, and
you definitely want to get your attack skill up to level eight because that's when you unlock special attacks. Special
attacks do more damage, and they're essential for surviving and thriving in Dragon Wilds on into the endame. Once
you've gotten the basics of melee combat down, you can also specialize in either magic or range. At level five in magic,
you will unlock secondary attacks. At level 16, you'll unlock Arcane Expertise, which provides automatic
combo finishers. The ranged equivalent of special attacks is trick shot, which you unlock at level eight ranged, and
that revolves around a rhythm-based perfect timing system. You will need to have a functioning base
before diving into magic or range, though, because these use runes and arrows or bolts, respectively, and
you'll have to make these in your base. To get started with magic, you'll need an ash battle staff, which you make
using planks from a sawmill and cloth from a loom. You can gather your basic starter runes, or you can make them with
the rune crafting skill. For range, you need to make an ash short bow with a fletching bench, and then also craft
arrows. That's basically all you need to know from when you're first getting started
with dragon wilds. The game does also have an intuitive quest system that will guide you through its narrative content,
but at each step of the way, you'll have to make better gear, improve your base,
etc. So, now that you know how to get in the game, how to make a base, and the different kinds of weapons you can use,
let's talk about some stuff you want to focus on as you prepare for the end game. Your first base will not be your last
base, or at least it shouldn't be. Starting with erecting basic outposts in every biome, you're eventually going to
want to relocate your main base to an endgame zone to take advantage of better materials and make your progression much
easier. But speaking of progression, one of the main goals of the game is leveling your
skills, and that remains one of the few things to do once you've tackled the rest of the endgame challenges. If there
are any particular skill lines you like more than others, focus on getting them to level 99 to unlock that skill's
iconic skill cape. There are also a variety of world events that remain relevant onto the endgame,
including roaming bosses who drop epic loot. And with the 1.0 release of Dragon Wilds, players can now access both rune
and dragon armor, which anyone who's played any Runescape games before should already be familiar with and know these
are the best types of armor in the game. So, keep on progressing through your crafting milestones until you can craft
rune armor. And with the four player Cauldra raid that's coming with 1.0, you'll be able to craft dragon armor.
The CER raid is the pinnacle content of the 1.0 release, but if you're brand new to the game, you're going to want to
spend a lot of time in Dragon Wilds if you're ready to do that. You're going to need the best armor, weapons, and food
to take on this godlike dragon boss. And that does it for the basics of knowing what you need to do first in
Runescape Dragon Wilds. I see these oneplus hour guides out there, and while I appreciate the time and dedication it
takes to make those, I also appreciate and respect your guys' time. So, I wanted to pack as much information in
here as I could while keeping the video relatively short and succinct. And my hope is that I got you started off in
Dragon Wilds on the right foot. So, thanks for watching. If there's anything that I didn't cover that you'd
like to know more about, please leave it in the comments along with any feedback
either on the game or on the video, plus any Dragon Wilds content you'd like to see. I will be streaming with my initial
reactions to the game later today, so definitely stop by if you have the time or check the recap. But I do plan to
continue covering this game as I play and enjoy it myself. So your comments and suggestions are very helpful. If you
appreciate the work I'm doing here, please do like and hype the video and subscribe if you haven't. And you can
support my work even further with a membership, a merch purchase, or a donation. While I'm so grateful to all
of you for supporting me, in the end, I'm even more grateful to God. So like I do in all my videos, we're going to
finish this video with a brief prayer to my Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. If you don't like that or makes you
uncomfortable, just skip ahead. Lord Jesus, thank you for making it possible to make this video today. Thank
you for inspiring Jagex to make Dragon Wilds. And I ask that you bless everyone's experiences in the game. I
ask you to bless this video and empower it to assist as many people as possible.
And Lord, I do pray for the growth of my channel. Lord Christ, please do bless everyone watching this video. Bless them
with your love, providence, and grace. Lord Jesus, I give you all glory for this video and for my channel. Lord, in
your mercy, here our prayer. Thanks again for watching. Please do like, hype, comment, and subscribe
before you go. And when you subscribe, turn on notifications cuz I'll be back soon with new content.
